title: Cost-anchored region slicing and heterogeneous accelerator prefetcher
creator: Sofia Alvarez
description: Design and implement a routing controller that slices global capacity by region/tier based on cost anchors and dynamically prefetches/allocates heterogeneous accelerators. The controller should prefer cheaper capacity (spot-like pools) when safe, automatically switch to on-demand families when budgets or SLO pressure require it, and select GPU families based on model latency/cost trade-offs. Enforce per-tenant and global spend caps and expose visibility in Console for engineers and SREs.
proposed_solution: 1) Introduce 'region slices' representing tunable capacity windows (e.g., cheap-tier, balanced-tier, fast-tier) per region. 2) Add a cost-aware allocator that scores candidate host pools using a composite metric: effective cost-per-token, historical preemption risk, and latency headroom. 3) Implement a prefetcher that warms KV-cache and small-batch allocator on selected heterogeneous GPU families (A100-int8, H100-quantized, etc.) based on model profile. 4) Attach soft budget caps per tenant and hard global shields; when caps breach, gracefully degrade to cached model variants or lower-precision replicas. 5) Integrate signals into Console for per-route cost burn and headroom metrics.
tradeoffs: Prefetching heterogeneous devices reduces tail latency but increases short-term spend; we mitigate by capping prefetch concurrency and TTL.
Relying on historical preemption risk may mispredict rapid market shifts; balanced by conservative decay and live telemetry.
Enforcing hard caps can cause request rejections; prefer staged degradations (model variant, quantized path, cached prefix) before reject.
Complex scoring increases allocator CPU overhead; we will optimize with caching of scores and async recompute windows.
acceptance_criteria: End-to-end allocation path routes 95% of eligible requests into cheaper-tier pools without increasing p95 latency by >10% compared to baseline.
Per-tenant soft budget warning triggers at 90% of cap; hard cap enforces reject or fallback with documented behaviour.
Console shows per-route cost burn and projected 24h spend with live headroom signal.
Fallback chain (variant -> quantized -> cached) keeps success rate >=99% under simulated spot eviction loads.

progress_updates: 2026-03-10: Kickoff meeting. Agreed on scoring inputs: cost-per-minute, preemption-rate, p95-latency-headroom.
2026-03-11: Prototype allocator scoring and simulated traffic harness created; initial results show 22% cost reduction for non-critical routes.
2026-03-12: Integrated soft-cap signalling into tenant budget store; observed false positives during bursty writes, added debounce to store updates.
review_feedback: PM (Michael): Ensure transparent customer options to opt-out of spot-preference; add tenant-level flag.
SRE (Lena): Request circuit-breaker for prefetcher to avoid thundering herd during region failover.
Security (Omar): Verify KMS-bound telemetry does not expose tenant identifiers in cost signals.
blockers: Missing quota API for per-tenant hard cap enforcement (depends on billing team endpoint).
Need a safe lab with heterogeneous GPU families for prefetch testing—current infra only exposes single family in staging.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (canary): Route 1% of non-SLA-critical routes, monitor cost and p95 latency for 72h.
Phase 2 (ramped): 10% then 30% with feature flags per-customer and tenant opt-out.
Phase 3 (global): Default enabled with conservative caps and auto-tuning for 7 days.
test_plan: Unit tests for scoring function with synthetic cost/preemption inputs.
Integration test: simulate spot eviction spike and verify fallback chain maintains >=99% success.
Load test: ensure allocator CPU overhead <5% of control under production-like QPS.
Chaos test: region outage simulation with prefetcher circuit-breaker enabled.
next_steps: Implement hard-cap enforcement API integration with billing (blocked by billing endpoint).
Stand up heterogenous-device lab for prefetch experiments (Infra).
Finalize prefetch TTL and concurrency knobs and add configurable defaults per release.
